title: Confirm Reference genome used for alignment?

latest.raw:
Hello SageBio team -

Thank you for running this hackathon. Would it be possible to share the reference genome file utilized for the alignment or at least confirm if it is publicly located and its MD5? Separately, is part of the challenge to make the tool agnostic to reference genome or can we make some assumptions based on the reference genome utilized?

Thank you,

Fadi

latest.raw:
Hi Fadi,

Thanks for the thoughtful questions!

Reference genome build: GRCh38. this is confirmed, as all variant coordinates in the underlying clinical report are given in GRCh38 

Exact reference FASTA / MD5: I don't have this confirmed on hand. Let me check with the team and follow up with the specifics.

On reference-genome agnosticism: since all provided data (variant coordinates, VCF) is in GRCh38, you're welcome to build your pipeline assuming GRCh38 — making your tool reference-agnostic isn't a requirement of this challenge. I'll confirm this is the intended design and follow up if that changes.

Thanks again for the careful attention to detail 

Best,
Gaia

latest.raw:
Hi Fadi, Gaia,

The exact FASTA is in the VCF header, so it can be confirmed without waiting on the team. The ##reference line in WGS_EX2312012_HGWCNDSX7.vcf.gz reads:

GCA_000001405.15_GRCh38_no_alt_analysis_set_plus_hs38d1_maskedGRC_exclusions_v2_no_chr.fasta

GRCh38, no-alt analysis set, hs38d1 decoy, masked GRC exclusions. Called with Sentieon 202308.02, then GATK VariantFiltration.

Two details from the same header that fail quietly if missed:

No chr prefix on contigs — they are 1, 2, … X, Y, with M for mitochondria. A fetch using chr15 returns an empty result rather than an error.
PGT/PID are present, so read-backed phasing is available. Relevant to your phasing point: the INFO AF field is the within-sample allele fraction with AN=2, not a population frequency — filtering on it for rarity removes nothing, silently.

python
import pysam
vcf = pysam.VariantFile("WGS_EX2312012_HGWCNDSX7.vcf.gz")
for line in str(vcf.header).split("\n"):
    if line.startswith("##reference"):
        print(line[:170])
print(list(vcf.header.contigs)[:5])

The header names the file but not its checksum, so the MD5 would still need the team.

Fernando

latest.raw:
Hi Fernando - appreciate you confirming. I wanted to verify with an MD5 rather than rely on file name. But I'll take your reply as confirmation that I can use this filename information exactly as-is in the header unless I hear otherwise from the team.

Thanks also for clarifying the phasing information and GRC exclusions. I'll use the NCBI file (https://ftp-trace.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/ReferenceSamples/giab/release/references/GRCh38/GCA_000001405.15_GRCh38_no_alt_analysis_set_maskedGRC_exclusions_v2.fasta.gz) as it closely matches the header file. You can probably tell by my questions that I'm looking at using the FASTQs to reconstruct regions around the variant calls from VCF. So, having all this information right affects indel reconstruction and other events around masked regions. I'm leaving this information here in case others want to use it.

If there are no changes, then there is no need for MD5 or further answers. This addresses my reference question. Thank you and the SageBio team for following up on this!

Fadi
